name: Utah
overview: Utah counties sell real property with delinquent taxes at an annual tax sale that the county auditor conducts in May or June. A property is offered once its period of redemption is expiring, which comes after the lapse of four years from the date the taxes became delinquent. Until then, anyone may redeem the property on behalf of the record owner at any time before the tax sale. Each county sets its own date, format and payment rules within that window.

counties.how_to_bid: Online only, through Public Surplus; register there. For the 2026 sale a refundable credit card deposit was charged at your first bid on each property ($50 for properties with a tax value of $10,000 or less, $100 above that); the deposit is not applied to the price. Winning bidders received emailed instructions and paid in full by wire transfer through Public Surplus within 5 business days; tax deeds are recorded and mailed in about 4 to 6 weeks. Property can be redeemed until the sale starts. The county advises calling the office to confirm wire details before sending money.

counties.how_to_bid: All bidders must preregister before the sale and get a bidder number; online sales also require registration with the auction company, and a bid deposit may be required. Bidding starts at the minimum bid (taxes, penalties, interest and administrative costs); in-person bids rise in $100 increments. Only cash or certified funds are accepted; for in-person sales full payment is due to the county treasurer before 4 pm the day of the sale. A $400 advertising and noticing fee applies per parcel. Bids are conditional until the County Council accepts them.

counties.how_to_bid: The sale is held entirely online at Public Surplus; bidders must register there before the day of the sale. Bidders may submit a credit card (VISA, MasterCard or Discover) once bidding opens, and the minimum bid charge is held on the card when the first bid is placed; the hold is released if you lose or after the winner wires the full winning bid. No bid below the total of taxes, interest, penalty and administrative costs is accepted. The Auditor's Office does not give technical support for the auction site. Properties are sold as is, where is.
